corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The reply candidly recognizes suffering as the strongest counterevidence, distinguishes substantial evidential pressure from a decisive defeater, and offers several specifically Christian considerations rather than denying the objection's seriousness. Principal limitation: The disordered world, afterlife, available theodicies, and divine participation are presented compactly without showing how they change the probability of particular apparently gratuitous horrors rather than merely demonstrate logical compatibility. Live burden: Edwards must connect each consideration to the evidential distribution and severity of suffering, explaining why an all-loving, all-powerful God would permit these cases and why compensatory goods are morally sufficient. Locked score: The very-strong band reflects exceptional relevance, calibration, explicit concession, and direct engagement with the central objection, while retaining a meaningful evidential limitation because the proposed responses are named more fully than their probabilistic mechanisms are defended.

corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The reply grants multiple positive arguments conditionally and then precisely exposes the inferential distance between establishing some creator and identifying the all-powerful, perfectly loving God targeted by the motion. Principal limitation: A sophisticated cumulative case can assign attributes jointly rather than expect any single design or moral argument to establish the complete classical conception, so the identity gap alone does not dispose of Edwards's combined evidence. Live burden: Woodford must show that apparently gratuitous suffering remains sufficiently improbable under the cumulative classical hypothesis, while Edwards must demonstrate how his arguments jointly identify the relevant attributes and reconcile them with evil. Locked score: The very-strong band reflects excellent conditional reasoning, stable scope, high responsiveness, and direct contact with several central claims, moderated only because the underlying gratuitousness premise and the cumulative identification question still require further comparative defense.
